**Rebuttal (Debater A)**

Debater B's case rests on the same unsupported footing it criticizes. "The literature supports this" cites no paper, names no pair of groups, and identifies no separating invariant. B also says that a failure of isoclinism must occur somewhere because isoclinism is the expected invariant. That shows an order where failure is plausible, not that it occurs at 32. Expecting a counterexample does not locate the smallest one.

I concede that my weakest link is the step from $B_0 \cong C_2$ to an isomorphism of conjugacy quandles. I have not verified that construction, and the solution does not establish it.

The burden is symmetric. B's claim needs an explicit non-isoclinic pair of order 32 with isomorphic conjugacy quandles, and my claim needs the absence of such pairs below 128. Neither has been shown. A computation over the SmallGroups library, comparing conjugacy quandle isomorphism classes and isoclinism classes for each order up to 128, would decide the question directly.

Until that check is done, I maintain 128. I will revise if a concrete pair of order-32 groups is produced that are non-isoclinic but have isomorphic conjugacy quandles.
